diagnosis:
I submitted model-4, calibrated with the DDS optimiser against daily NSE over 1971-1997 (the first year was warm-up). Calibration NSE is 0.79, KGE 0.67 and r 0.90. I did not run a split-sample validation, so I expect NSE in 1998-2008 to be somewhat lower, roughly 0.70-0.78.

The main weakness is a persistent overestimate of total flow (PBIAS +23%). Rainfall (1.76 mm/day) is high compared with the observed runoff (about 0.48 mm/day), and the model cannot evaporate or lose enough water to close that gap. To limit the damage, the optimiser picked a high LP (0.89) and a reduced snowfall correction (SFCF 0.76), and it represents this clay catchment as flashy: high BETA (7), FC about 310 mm and a fast upper store.

One alternative run scored a slightly higher NSE (0.80), but only because a near-zero K2 let the lower store slowly soak up water, which acts like a leak in the model. That store was still filling at the end of 1997, and once it is near equilibrium the bias gets worse (about 23-29%) and NSE drops to 0.79-0.80. So I set K2 to at least 0.005, which makes the lower store reach equilibrium within the warm-up year. The submitted set is therefore not sensitive to the starting storage levels.

Expect weaker results at low flows and in summer, and the high-flow volumes in the drier months will probably be too large. I am fairly confident in the overall behaviour but less sure of individual values: FC, LP and BETA trade off against each other, and the snow parameters barely matter because only about 2% of precipitation falls as snow.
